# scenario G3: Trip C offline
# argv: --trip-fixture trip_c_lon_mry_surcharge.json --offline --balance UR=160000 --card Chase Sapphire Preferred --transfer-date 2026-09-15 --show-alternatives
# exit: 0

TRIP C - the surcharge case (LON->MRY, plus a same-metal comparison)
C1 is Trip B's real LON->MRY leg, scored with the surcharge model. C2 is a constructed business-cabin leg that exercises the same-metal alternatives engine, which C1's economy cabin cannot.
Source: C1 transcribes the real LON->MRY capture (Google Flights, 2026-09-07, Tsuki). C2 is CONSTRUCTED for acceptance testing and is NOT a real captured itinerary - its award prices are 
labelled synthetic and must never be quoted as real.

Wallet (supplied at runtime - nothing is assumed)
  UR: 160,000   valued at 1.00 cents/point
  cards: Chase Sapphire Preferred

Transfer date: 2026-09-15 (ratios and bonuses are looked up on THIS date, not on the travel date - the ratio that applies is the one in force when you transfer)

==============================================================================
FX rates used (table as of 2026-09-08):
  1 EUR = 1.1620 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-07 (4 days old)   [BOOKING-SITE IMPLIED: back-derived from the Novotel Madrid dual-currency quote ($747.81 / EUR643.57 = 
1.1620). One booking page on one date - NOT a market rate.]
  1 GBP = 1.3540 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-08 (3 days old)   [SOURCED on 2026-09-08. Replaces the 1.2700 placeholder, which had no source and understated the London 
hotel by about $42. A sourced rate still goes stale - confirm before trusting.]
  1 CAD = 0.7256 USD [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]   sourced 2026-09-08 (3 days old)   [SOURCED on 2026-09-08. Added so the captured CAD 44.60 tax on the real SFO-MAD Aeroplan award can be 
scored instead of carried as an unknown. Confirm before trusting.]
  !! FX RATES REQUIRE CONFIRMATION. EUR is back-derived from a single hotel quote; GBP and CAD were looked up on a date and go stale. Every foreign-currency total below inherits that 
uncertainty.
  !! Supply a rate with --fx GBP=1.36 to take responsibility for it and clear the marker.
==============================================================================

Valuation: cash is scored at 1.00 cents per point ($1.00 cash = 100 points-equivalent). Points and cash are ranked on this single yardstick.

Data problems flagged, NOT silently fixed
  - C2 IS SYNTHETIC. Its points prices are invented for the purpose of exercising the alternatives engine and are labelled as such on every candidate. C1 is real captured data.
  - C1's British Airways option carries a carrier-imposed surcharge that was NOT captured. Scoring it as $0 would show a saving of roughly $282 that does not exist. The surcharge is modelled
as a range, never as zero.

Per-leg detail

C1 - LON->MRY, Jan 27 2027, one-way, economy, 1 adult (real capture; arrives SFO)
  Verdict: POINTS - Points path scores $280.00 vs $482.00 cash.
  Cash: $482 British Airways LHR-SFO nonstop 3:20pm-6:45pm, 11h25
  Points: United LHR-SFO nonstop (badge 27.6k pts)
        UR 28,000 -> United MileagePlus 28,000 @ 1:1 [Chase Sapphire Preferred]
        spend: 28,000 UR
        stranded: 400 (within the unavoidable transfer increment)
        metal: UA (source: captured), cabin Y
  Surcharge: $0.00  via United MileagePlus / metal=* / * / cabin=* / dep=*
        source: project research seed table 2026-09-08 - NOT corroborated against a published source
        PROGRAM POLICY not a route observation. United does not pass carrier-imposed surcharges through on awards. Government taxes and airport charges including UK APD are still owed and 
are NOT modelled here.
  Margin: points save $63.89 (13.3% of the cash price)
  note: This is Trip B's B4 leg, isolated so the surcharge behaviour can be pinned by a test.
  note: Departing LHR is the worst case in the surcharge model: UK Air Passenger Duty stacks on top of the carrier-imposed surcharge.
  FLAG: NO option actually arrives MRY. All arrive SFO. Return positioning SFO->Monterey is unpriced.
  FLAG: The economy surcharge for British Airways ex-LHR is NOT in the model. The research behind data/surcharges.csv is business-cabin only, and economy figures were deliberately not 
extrapolated from it.
  UNVERIFIED: Surcharge note: PROGRAM POLICY not a route observation. United does not pass carrier-imposed surcharges through on awards. Government taxes and airport charges including UK APD
are still owed and are NOT modelled here.
  UNVERIFIED: Points price for United LHR-SFO nonstop (badge 27.6k pts) is UNVERIFIED (google_badge_unverified). Google Flights '27.6k pts' badge. UNVERIFIED. United levies no 
carrier-imposed surcharge as a matter of program policy, which is why this resolves to a confirmed $0. UK departure taxes are still owed and are NOT modelled.
  UNVERIFIED: Program attribution for United LHR-SFO nonstop (badge 27.6k pts) -> United MileagePlus is an ASSUMPTION; the source did not name the program.
  UNVERIFIED: British Airways LHR-SFO nonstop (badge 20k pts): NOT SCORED - its carrier-imposed surcharge is UNKNOWN (not $0). At 20,000 UR its cost floor is $200.00 before any surcharge, 
against $280.00 for the option chosen above.
  UNVERIFIED: SAME ROUTE, DIFFERENT PROGRAM, NO CARRIER SURCHARGE: United MileagePlus carries $0 in carrier-imposed surcharge here as a matter of program policy, while British Airways 
Executive Club could not be scored at all because its surcharge on this metal is unknown. Government taxes and airport charges are still owed on both and are not modelled.
  APD: UK AIR PASSENGER DUTY on C1: this leg DEPARTS GB for US. ADDED to the points-side cash total: GBP 102.00 x 1 = GBP 102.00 = $138.11 per the reduced rate. Band B chosen because HMRC 
bands by distance from London to the DESTINATION COUNTRY'S CAPITAL: Washington DC, 3665 miles. APD is owed on award tickets too and does not care which program or which airline; the captured
CASH fare already contains it, which is why it is added to the points side only. Source: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rates-and-allowances-for-air-passenger-duty. The GBP->USD conversion 
above is marked [CONFIRM BEFORE TRUSTING]; this APD figure inherits that uncertainty.

C2 - SYNTHETIC: JFK->DUB, business, on Aer Lingus metal, priced in British Airways Executive Club
  Verdict: CASH (SURCHARGE UNKNOWN) - A points path exists (British Airways Executive Club, 50,000 points) but the carrier-imposed surcharge on this metal is UNKNOWN, so it cannot be scored 
against $1,800.00 cash. It is NOT $0, and it must not be treated as $0. Points win only if the surcharge is below $1,300.00.
  Cash: SYNTHETIC $1,800 business fare JFK-DUB
  Points: SYNTHETIC BA Executive Club award on Aer Lingus metal, JFK-DUB business
        UR 50,000 -> British Airways Executive Club 50,000 @ 1:1 [Chase Sapphire Preferred]
        spend: 50,000 UR
        metal: EI (source: captured), cabin J
  Surcharge: UNKNOWN - this is NOT $0.
        Break-even: points beat cash only if the surcharge is below $1,300.00.
        Cannot model a surcharge for 'SYNTHETIC BA Executive Club award on Aer Lingus metal, JFK-DUB business'. No surcharge rule for British Airways Executive Club on EI metal, NA-EU J 
departing US. This is NOT zero - the figure is simply not known.
  note: CONSTRUCTED CASE, not a capture. It exists to exercise alternatives.find_same_metal_alternatives(): the same EI aeroplane can be ticketed in Aer Lingus AerClub, whose surcharge band 
IS modelled, while BA Executive Club's surcharge on EI metal is not.
  FLAG: SYNTHETIC POINTS PRICE. 50,000 Avios is invented for this test and is not a real award price.
  UNVERIFIED: Points price for SYNTHETIC BA Executive Club award on Aer Lingus metal, JFK-DUB business is UNVERIFIED (synthetic_test_fixture). SYNTHETIC. Invented for acceptance testing. 
Never quote this number.
  UNVERIFIED: SYNTHETIC BA Executive Club award on Aer Lingus metal, JFK-DUB business: the carrier-imposed surcharge is UNKNOWN, so this points option CANNOT be scored against cash. It is 
NOT $0. Points beat cash only if the surcharge is below $1,300.00.

C2 - same-metal alternatives
  Aer Lingus AerClub on EI metal - surcharge $60-$100 (pt $75)
    UNPRICED counterfactual: beats the option above if its award price is below 172,500 points. NOT scored - go look it up.
    Bookability inferred from alliance membership, not from a verified partnership. Confirm before relying on it.
    Aer Lingus AerClub can ticket EI metal and carries $60-$100 (pt $75) in carrier-imposed surcharge, where British Airways Executive Club's surcharge on this metal is UNKNOWN. Award price 
NOT known - look it up. NOTE: Aer Lingus AerClub and British Airways Executive Club spend the SAME Avios but price awards from DIFFERENT charts. Do not assume the British Airways Executive 
Club price applies.

NO leg was scored against live availability. The points prices here come from: google_badge_unverified, synthetic_test_fixture - a MIX. The google_badge_unverified ones are Google Flights 
badges, of which exactly one has ever been corroborated. This is not a live margin.

The headline above is a RANGE and must not be quoted as a single number. The spread is carrier-imposed surcharges that are not known. The low end is what the tool can defend today; the high 
end assumes every unknown surcharge turns out to be $0, which is the assumption that turns an unknown into a saving that is not there.
